_what_this_is: Diffs that changed something which CHECKS the work -- test files, CI/hook configuration, or push-gate logic. A flag is NOT a finding and NOT a refusal. It is a record that an agent edited its own checker, written so a reviewer can ask why without having to notice it first.
_what_it_does_NOT_claim: That the edit was wrong, or that an unflagged edit was fine. See blind_spots: an assertion that still exists and tests nothing is invisible here.
blind_spots: An assertion that still EXISTS and no longer tests anything. The count holds, the sense is inverted, and nothing here can see it.
A fixture quietly made easier. The arms all still run and all still pass.
A weakening spread across two pushes, where neither diff alone matches a shape. This reads one outgoing range at a time.
Intent. It reports SHAPE. A deleted arm may be a correct deletion of a wrong arm -- which is exactly why this flags and does not block.

CODE versus PROSE ABOUT CODE, and this is MEASURED rather than feared. On its own landing commit -- the first real diff it ever saw -- the WEAKENING level was 3 of 3 FALSE: the word "ignored" inside a probe assertion label, a comment saying "silent skip", and this file's own _BOUND_HINTS tuple. Dropping comment lines took it to 2 of 3, and BOTH SURVIVORS ARE STILL FALSE -- prose inside a STRING LITERAL, which is real code by every syntactic test. SO THE WEAKENING LEVEL IS A TRIAGE PROMPT AND NOT A FINDING, on an n of 1 real push. It is left matching rather than narrowed, per scrubber item 24: narrowing clears the known instance and fails silently on the next phrasing, and in a detector a false negative is invisible where a false positive is loud and gets read. The rate on a larger sample is still unmeasured.

COVERAGE OF THE CLASS LIST ITSELF. A path in no SELF_CHECKING class is not examined and is not reported. The push-gate-logic class is a NAMED LIST of seven files, not a glob -- a new checker nobody adds to it is invisible here, which is the same staleness this platform keeps paying for one level up.

So a row asserted that the tip commit changed files it does not contain, while the commit that really changed them got no row. They are 3 distinct paths re-keyed against 7 shas -- the same push refused and rewritten six times. 6 of the 7 shas are ORPHANED in hank's OWN clone (verified there, not inferred from absence here). The 7th, bf174f30, resolves and is an ancestor of origin/main, and its 3 rows are still WRONG: it changes five docs files and NONE of the three paths they name. Subject-matching the orphans to their landed replacements is provably ambiguous -- two orphans share the subject "the three records this batch's fixes owe" and no landed commit carries it -- so no re-seat was attempted and none was guessed. BACKFILLED FROM THE REAL COMMITS INSTEAD, which is stronger than copying a stashed row: the classifier was run against each landed commit's OWN diff. The 20 rows reduce to FOUR facts -- 320ddabe tests/run_tool_usage_refusal_probe.py WEAKENING, 72d757ef tests/run_audit_event_type_probe.py WEAKENING, 4ec0d5d5 and 56bbce5e tests/sd_data_write_attribution_three_apps.js CHANGE. FIXED IN THE GENERATOR: tools/sairn_push_gate_hook.py now keys per COMMIT from that commit's own diff, and prints COULD NOT ATTRIBUTE rather than keying to the tip when no single commit produces the flags. _corrected_2026_10_08b: FORTY-EIGHT ROWS REMOVED AS PROVABLY FALSE, and a validator added so this cannot accumulate again. The 2026-10-08 correction above fixed the GENERATOR -- flags are now keyed per commit from that commit's own diff -- and said plainly that it was NOT retroactive. This is the retroactive half, done with a check rather than by hand. MEASURED by tools/scrutiny_ledger_check.py over all 114 rows: HOLDS 24, CONTRADICTED 30, MERGE_KEYED 18, UNRESOLVABLE 42, MALFORMED 0, duplicate identities 0. The 48 findings were removed; the 24 that hold and the 42 that cannot be checked in this clone were kept. CONTRADICTED means the sha resolves, is a single-parent commit, and its diff for that path is EMPTY -- the row accuses a commit of a change it does not contain. MERGE_KEYED IS REPORTED SEPARATELY AND THAT MATTERS: `git show` prints no diff for a merge commit, so an empty result there proves nothing either way, and calling it a contradiction would be a true sentence pointing at the wrong cause -- the same misdiagnosis fixed in the D9 gate message this same day. A merge authors no change, so it is never the commit in which a checker was edited; the row is wrong for that reason instead. The dropped rows were overwhelmingly keyed to merge commits, handoff commits and bookkeeping commits -- i.e. to push TIPS -- which is the signature of the defect the generator fix removed. NOTHING TRUE WAS LOST: a row whose named commit does not contain the named change is false, and deleting a false row discards no information. What IS still missing is the flags those pushes really owed, and they are not recoverable from here -- the same disclosure the 2026-10-08 note already carries. UNRESOLVABLE IS NOT A FINDING AND IS KEPT: a row can legitimately name a commit this clone has never fetched, and a validator that failed on one would be out of the merge policy within a week. VALIDATOR NOW DECLARED in merge_policy, which closes the gap that made tools/sairn_rebase_resolve.py exit 2 on this file's conflicts and forced a hand merge on 2026-10-08.

_resolution_policy: A resolution is a REVIEW RECORD attached to a flag, never a deletion of one. The flag row stays exactly as the gate wrote it, including its level, so a reader sees what fired as well as what was concluded. A resolution written by the commit AUTHOR must say so in its status field and must carry a reproduction command, because an author verdict is worth only as much as the measurement anybody else can re-run. Added 2026-10-13 (cody, b7) with the first resolution; the schema is additive and the validator tools/scrutiny_ledger_check.py keys on (sha, path) only, so an extra key does not affect union-by-identity merges.
